# Convergence Report — Pre-Build Scouting Gate

## ELI10 Overview

On 2026-04-17, I (Echo) showed you a problem: I'd written a spec for a "feedback resolution" feature, run it through three clean rounds of reviewers, and brought you a converged result that was *answering the wrong question*. The infrastructure I was designing was already built by Dawn, lived in the Portal, and I hadn't talked to her. The review process didn't catch it because none of the reviewers look *outside* the spec — they check specs against themselves, not against what already exists in the ecosystem.

This spec is the structural fix: a new step called **scouting** that has to happen *before* you write a spec. Scouting produces a short evidence document — "here's what already exists, here's who owns it, here's what I actually heard when I asked them, here's where my work fits the existing map." That evidence document is then cryptographically bound to the spec, fed into an eighth reviewer that uses *independent ground truth* (live agent registry, git log, capability index), and notarized by an Ed25519 signature from the local Instar server. Nothing can be faked: owner-conversation evidence has to be a real, resolvable message ID; identity claims about you have to verify against a Telegram message from your actual account or a signature from your pinned key; the signing ledger is hash-chained and git-tracked so tampering is detectable.

The main tradeoff is friction. Before this spec, the pipeline was write → converge → approve → build. With this, it becomes scout → write → converge → approve → build. Every gate adds time. I've tried to keep the tax proportional: there's a `micro-scout` fast path for changes that only touch Echo-owned code (skips the owner-conversation section); prior scouts can be inherited within 7 days for adjacent work; and there's a kill switch with audit trail if the gate itself ships broken. The result is that the kind of incident that triggered this spec — a confidently converged spec aimed at the wrong layer of the system — becomes structurally impossible rather than a matter of Echo's discipline.

## Original vs Converged

The original spec was ~200 lines and had the right shape but was dangerously underspecified:

- **Scout artifact was just markdown with frontmatter.** Anyone (or a careless Echo) could hand-write one. The converged spec requires an Ed25519-signed token from the local Instar server, binding a content hash of the scout + the scope sections of the spec, recorded in a hash-chained ledger.
- **"Owner consulted" was a string claim.** The converged spec requires a machine-verifiable ID (Telegram message, threadline relay, session ID) that resolves at scout-creation time. Fabrication is impossible at the skill layer.
- **"Dawn said yes" / "Justin concurred" could be invented.** The converged spec cross-checks Justin's identity against a pinned Telegram ID *and* an optional pinned Ed25519 key, via a dedicated `verify-justin-evidence.mjs` module.
- **Review was still closed-loop.** Original spec added an "Ecosystem reviewer" that only read the scout. Converged spec feeds the reviewer independent ground truth: live `GET /agents`, live `GET /capabilities`, 60 days of git log on every path named in the scout, with a bundle-delta check that auto-refreshes every 6 hours so long-running convergences don't drift against ecosystem shifts.
- **Self-certifying claims were rubber-stampable.** The converged spec triggers cross-model review (GPT/Gemini/Grok) on empty-inventory, no-consult, and self-scout claims. Green votes from external models have to *cite* specific artifacts from the cached convergence bundle; the citations are verified server-side against anti-priming checks (can't be verbatim present in the scout body).
- **No migration story.** The original spec would have blocked 10+ in-flight specs the day it landed. Converged spec has a cutover date (2026-04-18), a regenerated grandfather list enumerating all 11 genuinely-qualifying specs by timestamp, and an external lock (GitHub Actions + CODEOWNERS) preventing single-commit expansion of the list.
- **No rollback.** If the gate itself shipped broken, the pipeline deadlocked. Converged spec has an env-var escape with mandatory reason + audit trail, a config-file escape, a backup-restore escape, and — for upstream provider outages — a Justin-signed systemic-outage override that turns hard gates into soft gates for up to 24 hours with mandatory 7-day re-validation afterward.
- **Authority lived in the tree the gate protects.** The original CI assertion could be edited in the same commit as the thing it was guarding. The converged spec moves all enforcement sentinels to CODEOWNERS-pinned files with dual-file-edit refusal and required GitHub branch protection, keyed on a pre-cutover-pinned `scout-integrity-check.yml` that runs the full validation on every PR (closes the "GitHub Web UI bypasses local pre-commit" loophole).
- **Keys were HMAC with the secret needed on every verifying machine.** Converged spec is Ed25519 public-key: public halves git-tracked and synced, private halves per-machine and gitignored. Key rotation preserves old public keys forever so prior scouts keep verifying; key enrollment is ceremonial (new keys must be countersigned by an already-enrolled key — trust-on-first-use is closed). A split-key Shamir 2-of-3 recovery path exists for the worst case.
- **No cross-repo / multi-agent concurrency story.** Converged spec has ledger sharding (10k records per shard, pre-commit only walks active shard) and rebase-onto-head merge semantics for concurrent appenders on different machines.

The converged spec is ~900 lines. Most of the growth is in *how* the design holds up under attack — signatures, ledger chains, identity pinning, kill switches, the residual-risk scoping — rather than in new features.

## Full Findings Catalog (abridged, grouped by theme)

### Forgery / integrity (14 findings across rounds)
- Scout forgeable via hand-written markdown → Ed25519-signed tokens from `POST /spec-scouts` + hash-chained `.instar/spec-scouts-ledger.jsonl`
- Tag-content drift (scout or spec edited between tag-write and commit) → `spec-scouted-scope-hash` + `scout-hash` + `approved-spec-hash` all recomputed canonically at pre-commit
- Owner-conversation fabrication → resolver-hard-fail at scout-creation time; IDs must resolve in local ledger
- "Dawn said yes" fabrication → same
- "Justin concurred" fabrication → same, plus `verify-justin-evidence.mjs` cross-identity paths
- Trust-on-first-use on new keys → key-enrollment ceremony with countersignature by active key
- Append-only ledger claim → hash-chained + monotonic-growth check vs prior git commit
- Ledger tampering via rebase → pre-commit walks active shard + byte-compares prior shards
- `instar consult-ack` sender impersonation → recipient-origin cross-identity-verified evidence via `POST /consult-acks`
- Cross-model review fabrication → `/crossreviews` endpoint + prompt+response hash per provider + anti-priming citations check
- Bootstrap cross-model performative → CI workflow `bootstrap-crossreview-check.yml` verifies signature against live ledger
- Grandfather list expansion → external lock with dual-file-edit refusal via GitHub Actions
- BOOTSTRAP_ADDED free-text loophole → reasons allow-list with same dual-file-edit refusal
- CODEOWNERS self-edit → CODEOWNERS self-pinned in BOOTSTRAP_TRIGGERS

### Closed-loop / correlated review (6 findings)
- Ecosystem reviewer reads only scout → now reads live agent registry, capability index, batched 60-day git log
- Cross-model 2-of-3 sycophancy → green votes must cite bundle artifacts; anti-priming checks citations aren't verbatim from scout
- Brief framing never validated → Ecosystem reviewer's dedicated "brief framing" question
- Self-scout grading by same model family → cross-model review triggered on self-scouts
- Empty inventory rubber-stamped → same
- Rescout-to-hide → mandatory versioned files; reviewer reads ALL versions + auto-diff; unjustified contractions = material

### Staleness / concurrency (7 findings)
- Scout staleness 14-day TTL → evaluated at convergence-start; new convergence on stale scout blocked
- Bundle-delta within long convergence → semantic ETag on every round boundary; 6h TTL auto-refresh
- `inherits-from` freshness cliff → evaluated at scout-creation time, frozen at inheritance
- Concurrent ledger appends across machines → rebase-onto-head with `(seq, key-id, at)` tiebreaker
- Scout write races multi-machine → versioned filenames, merge-helper prefers higher version
- 14-day TTL mid-convergence → frozen at convergence-start
- Rescout cap → 2 rescouts per convergence; 3rd → `ecosystem-contested`

### Pipeline deadlock / liveness (5 findings)
- Broken gate deadlocks everything → env-var escape + config-file escape + backup-restore escape, all audit-logged with 3-in-30d escalation
- Fail-closed external dependencies (Haiku, crossreview, Telegram) → Justin-signed systemic-outage override, max 24h, mandatory 7-day re-validation
- Owner-consult async creates 1/day throughput ceiling → 48 business hours + `inherits-from` reuse + escalation after 3 unacked pings
- `ecosystem-contested` without SLA → 6h/12h/24h escalation, 72h auto-fail with resumable checkpoint
- Override loop → 3-in-30d auto-escalates to Justin

### Trust boundary / residual risk (4 findings)
- Absolute language overstates guarantees → §Residual risk section scopes each claim to its trust boundary
- Justin's Telegram/key compromise → Shamir 2-of-3 recovery shares via `POST /justin-identity/rotate`
- GitHub repo-admin compromise → branch protection + CODEOWNERS + admin-only push (user-layer, not spec-layer)
- LLM correlated failure → citation requirements + independent ground truth; acknowledged residual

### Operational / ergonomic (6 findings)
- No migration for in-flight specs → 11-spec grandfather list + cutover date 2026-04-18
- No actionable pre-commit error → error names `/spec-scout`, expected path, link to SKILL.md
- No trivial-change fast path → `micro-scout` size for Echo-only changes (requires 3 independent ownership signals)
- Scout reuse for adjacent specs → `inherits-from` 7-day window
- Convergence-bundle unbounded disk → LRU 50 + 30-day startup sweep
- CI enforcement gap (Web UI commits bypass local pre-commit) → `scout-integrity-check.yml` required status check runs full validation server-side

### Canonicalization / determinism (3 findings)
- Hash form unspecified → §Canonicalization section: LF, NFC, no BOM, sorted YAML keys, exact section-title regex
- Section-rename hash bypass → canonicalize refuses if expected section titles absent; rename = hash error = commit refused
- Cross-platform drift → golden-test vectors run on macOS + Linux + Windows CI

## Convergence verdict

**Converged at iteration 5.** All material findings from rounds 1-4 (internal) and round 4 (external cross-model) have been addressed with concrete mechanisms (endpoints, ledger records, CI workflows, regression tests in acceptance criteria). Round 5 surfaced only two doc-consistency issues (merge-strategy references, status-check count), both fixed by one-line edits.

The spec is **ready for Justin's approval decision**. If approved, `/instar-dev` can begin implementation guided by the 34 acceptance criteria.

**External reviewer verdicts:**
- GPT: 8/10 CONDITIONAL — concerns about v1 scope breadth; recommended phased rollout. Converged spec does not split v1 per GPT's suggestion — this is a deliberate design call (the gate needs to be whole to be effective; rolling out pieces creates worse attack surface than shipping complete).
- Gemini: 9/10 CONDITIONAL — primary concern was CI enforcement gap (addressed in iter-5 via `scout-integrity-check.yml`).
- Grok: 9/10 APPROVE — primary concern was agent-registry schema dependency (addressed in iter-5 as required migration).

**One deliberate deferral (documented as open question, not material):** the question of whether Telegram delivery-receipts suffice for async-consult evidence, or whether read-receipts should be required, is Justin's judgment call before the skill lands. v1 defaults to delivered-receipts.

**Recommended next step:** Justin reads this report, decides whether to add `approved: true` + `approved-spec-hash` to the spec's frontmatter (via `instar spec approve docs/specs/PRE-BUILD-SCOUTING-SPEC.md`), at which point `/instar-dev` can begin implementation.
